turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (PATIENT): Sorry I'm late in. The bus from Blanchardstown was desperate, I was standing half the way.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): You're grand. Sit yourself down, we'll get to you.

[SEG0003] person_1 (PATIENT): It's just my brother Declan was told last year he had kidney stones, and the woman next door said if the pain is in the back don't be hanging about. I nearly talked myself out of coming.
[SEG0004] person_2 (DOCTOR): The neighbour can say what she likes. What has actually brought you in today?
[SEG0005] person_1 (PATIENT): I woke at two... no, it was four in the morning, I checked the phone. Desperate pain in my left side, going down into the groin. And there's blood in the urine.
[SEG0006] person_2 (DOCTOR): Mm. How bad is the pain if you score it out of ten?
[SEG0007] person_1 (PATIENT): Err, around a seven out of ten. It comes in waves, grabs and lets go. It eased a small bit sitting here but it's still savage.
[SEG0008] person_2 (DOCTOR): And the blood, when did you see that?
[SEG0009] person_1 (PATIENT): First time I went to the toilet after I got up. The urine was pink. Proper blood. Scared the life out of me.
[SEG0010] person_2 (DOCTOR): Did you vomit at all?
[SEG0011] person_1 (PATIENT): Yeah. The once, around half four. Nothing since.
[SEG0012] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any fever, or shivers?
[SEG0013] person_1 (PATIENT): No. No fever, no shivers.
[SEG0014] person_2 (DOCTOR): Burning when you pass urine, or running to the toilet more than usual?
[SEG0015] person_1 (PATIENT): No burning. I'm going the normal amount.
[SEG0016] person_2 (DOCTOR): And the rest of you, chest and breathing, any cough or shortness of breath?
[SEG0017] person_1 (PATIENT): No. Chest is grand, breathing is fine.
[SEG0018] person_1 (PATIENT): Is it cancer, doctor? My head is going ninety with it.

[SEG0019] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'm not going to call this cancer off this story, and I won't lock a diagnosis in yet. What fits is a stone in the tube from the kidney, or a kidney infection. I'm holding both until we see the tests. Either of those, not a conclusion.
[SEG0020] person_2 (DOCTOR): Let me feel your tummy. Left loin is tender to press. Abdomen is soft, there's no guarding.
[SEG0021] person_1 (PATIENT): Tender. Does that mean something's burst?
[SEG0022] person_2 (DOCTOR): No. A tender loin and a soft tummy is what this pain does. Nothing there says anything has burst.
[SEG0023] person_3 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Sorry, I've the obs and the dip when you want them.
[SEG0024] person_2 (DOCTOR): Go on, please.

[SEG0025] person_3 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Blood pressure 148 over 92, pulse 88, temperature 36.7, oxygen 98 percent. Urine dip shows blood three plus, protein a trace, leucocytes negative, nitrites negative.
[SEG0026] person_2 (DOCTOR): Grand. Thanks.

[SEG0027] person_2 (DOCTOR): So, back to you. Pain from four this morning, left side into the groin, around seven out of ten, in waves. One vomit. Visible blood, and the dip agrees, with no nitrite or leucocytes. No fever.
[SEG0028] person_1 (PATIENT): Of. So the dip means it isn't an infection?
[SEG0029] person_2 (DOCTOR): It makes infection less likely. It doesn't fully clear it. That's why I'm not concluding.
[SEG0030] person_1 (PATIENT): Do you need my tablets? I've the boxes in the bag.
[SEG0031] person_2 (DOCTOR): Yes, go through them.
[SEG0032] person_1 (PATIENT): Omprazole for the heartburn. I was on twenty milligrams, no, that's the old dose, it's forty milligrams once a day now.
[SEG0033] person_2 (DOCTOR): Forty milligrams of omprazole, once daily. Next?
[SEG0034] person_1 (PATIENT): Umm. Metformine for the sugar. Five hundred... no, a thousand milligrams, twice a day. I always say the old one.
[SEG0035] person_2 (DOCTOR): A thousand of metformine, twice a day. And for the blood pressure?
[SEG0036] person_1 (PATIENT): Mizartan, forty milligrams in the morning. Been on it a few years.
[SEG0037] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any allergies to medicines, aspirin, or anti-inflammatories?
[SEG0038] person_1 (PATIENT): No. No allergies at all.
[SEG0039] person_1 (PATIENT): Will I need an operation? I drive a van for work, I can't just be out.
[SEG0040] person_2 (DOCTOR): A lot of stones pass on their own, no operation. I can't promise that until the scan shows the size. Work can wait a day or two.
[SEG0041] person_1 (PATIENT): Is the scan the tunnel yoke? I'm a small bit claustrophobic. Will I be grand in it?
[SEG0042] person_2 (DOCTOR): It's a CT of the kidneys and ureters, a CT KUB. A few minutes, not a long lie-in. We'll book it for this afternoon, it's arranged.
[SEG0043] person_1 (PATIENT): And can you give me something for the pain? It's coming back up on me.
[SEG0044] person_2 (DOCTOR): Yes. Diclofenac, 75 milligrams, one injection here in the clinic before the scan. That should settle it.
[SEG0045] person_1 (PATIENT): Is that alright with the Mizartan and the Metformine? I was reading things.
[SEG0046] person_2 (DOCTOR): One dose is reasonable alongside them. Stay on your own tablets as usual. Don't add any extra anti-inflammatory at home on top of this.

[SEG0047] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'll see you back here on Friday and we'll go through the result. If the pain gets unbearable, or you can't keep fluids down, or a fever starts, go to A&E and don't wait till Friday.
[SEG0048] person_1 (PATIENT): Right. Friday. Can I drive the van tomorrow if it eases?
[SEG0049] person_2 (DOCTOR): No. Rest today and tomorrow. Driving with this pain isn't safe. We'll sort the work question on Friday.
[SEG0050] person_1 (PATIENT): Okay. Thanks. I'm still a bit all over the place, but okay.
[SEG0051] person_2 (DOCTOR): You're in the right place. The injection and the scan are both for today, and I'll see you Friday.

spec.situation: Sudden severe loin pain going to the groin overnight, vomiting once, blood in urine; pain score given loosely; urine dip result read aloud; painkiller and scan planned today.

traps.happens: The transcript looks like speech-to-text: drug names are sometimes spelled wrongly ('Omprazole', 'Mizartan' for telmisartan, 'Metformine'), fragments and fillers appear ('Err', 'Of.', 'Mm.', 'Umm'), numbers are sometimes digits and sometimes words.
traps.label_rule: Medicine names are recorded as written in the transcript (name) with a normalized/generic name ONLY when the true drug is certain from context (a drug 'for the pressure' written 'Mizartan' is NOT certain enough: leave generic_name empty). Fragments and fillers are never facts.

traps.happens: The conversation OPENS with a remark, joke, apology for being late, small talk, or a trigger event (a relative's diagnosis, a neighbour's advice, the receptionist's note) BEFORE the real reason is stated. The patient states the real concern a few turns later.
traps.label_rule: chief_complaint is the real concern in a short phrase in the patient's wording (e.g. 'worried about diabetes', 'voice gets tired'). NOT the opening remark, the joke or the trigger (the relative's illness goes into family_history only if it is a relative's condition said as such).

features: doctor_thinks_aloud: the doctor lists possible causes or says what they will not conclude yet. Only record a clinical assessment if the doctor actually states a leading or differential impression; 'let's see what the tests say' is not an assessment.
self_correction: a speaker states a number, drug name or duration and then corrects it in the same turn or later ('seventy-five... no, hundred and fifty'). The label holds only the corrected value.

bad.reason: Urine dipstick was completed, but transcript does not say clinical staff requested it.

omissions.text: Visible haematuria was described as pink urine / 'proper blood' the first time after getting up.
Negative findings asked and answered: no cough and no shortness of breath / chest and breathing fine.
Urine dipstick was also interpreted by the doctor as making infection less likely but not excluding it.
Doctor advised the patient to stay on usual tablets as normal alongside the single diclofenac dose.
Planned diclofenac was specifically a 75 mg injection given here in the clinic before the scan.
Follow-up plan included that the Friday visit would be to go through the scan result.
Doctor stated that both the injection and the scan were for today.
